name: Fence
constraints: DIRECTIONAL - requires alignTexture on the path; author width 0.40; the profile scale is NOT free
notes: ⭐ The FIRST directional tile: WRONG unless its path authors alignTexture true, which turns the tile along the path AND registers it across the path. Generated by tools/make-fence-tile.mjs, the fifth technique family. ⛔ The first cut was OPAQUE and read as a boardwalk (PO: not like a fence at all) - because registration did not exist yet, so nothing could sit at a known height across the ribbon, and A FENCE IS MOSTLY GAPS. It is now RGBA, alone among the ground tiles: a thin rail with posts standing proud of it and grass showing through. ⚑ The tile PIXEL HEIGHT is load-bearing - fence in the middle 48 of 96 rows, so width 0.40 reveals exactly the fence; safe to 0.80. Posts every 2.08 u. No baked shadow (the tile turns with its path). Author one path per straight leg.

name: Road
constraints: seamless-tiling; reads under blend mask; sits on land colour #006030
notes: Every road in the game. GENERATED placeholder (tools/make-cellular-tiles.mjs, the cellular family's third tile): packed brown earth with two warm grades of pebble pressed into it and hairline dried-mud cracks, all of it DELIBERATELY QUIET. ⛔ It USED TO BORROW pd106, the DESERT tile, so every lane was golden sandstone - that was the whole brief. ⛑ Three faults worth not repeating, all of them only visible once the tile REPEATS: too few slow bed waves paint a diagonal corduroy stripe; a neutral-grey pebble reads BLUE against warm brown; and mud cracks as a ridged field make closed loops that read as worm trails until they are thin and faint. ⛔ NO CART RUTS - a rut is directional and would need alignTexture, which wants one path per straight leg, and all three Road paths are multi-point meanders. Ruts are a second tile. ⭐ It ships at a SIXTH of its first pass' detail (PO: reads a little messy) - a ground tile is looked THROUGH, not at, and every mark repeats nine times across a screen, so one that looks slightly empty alone is the one that is right in the world. Real art wanted.

name: Dead tree
constraints: no-rotation; shadow may be baked in
notes: ⭐ The strongest silhouette in the forest set, and it is free: a LIVING tree from above is an opaque disc of leaves that hides its own structure, and a dead one IS the structure - the only forest prop that is neither round nor green. ⭐ The CAST SHADOW is the asset, not decoration: a flat branch diagram on flat ground reads as a crack in the earth, so the same limb geometry is drawn twice through <use> (never copied - a shadow out of step with its branches is worse than none), plus a third scaled-up pass for the dark outline, because a <use> cannot widen the strokes it references. ⛔ Collider 0.33 against a 0.95 visual - BRANCHES ARE AIR; blocking to the drip line would make it the most obstructive prop in the game while looking like the most passable. name: Stump
constraints: no-rotation; shadow may be baked in
notes: Cut stump - reads as people work here at a farm edge and as decay in the forest. Placeholder SVG (body r0.55, collider 0.41: the root flare and the chips are art, not obstacle). ⭐ It has to say CUT, not BROKEN, and the rings do not do that - three things do: the FELLING NOTCH biting in from the rim (a snapped tree has a ragged spike, a felled one a clean V), the SAW KERF (straight parallel lines at one angle, indifferent to the centre, crossing the concentric rings), and the CHIPS thrown onto the grass. Rings are 2px off-centre or they read as a machined target. ⛔ The thick DARK BARK RING is load-bearing: haystack.svg was misread as a stump once, because a pale disc with radial lines IS a stump - the rim is what tells them apart.

name: Fallen log
owner: C2b) - its baked shadow turns with it; preserveAspectRatio=none
column18: ⭐ What makes it a log rather than a BEAM is that the two ends do not match: one sawn (end grain, rings off-centre) and one TORN (splinters past where the bark stops). Two identical ends is milled timber. The sawn end also makes it stump.svg's partner - the stump is the bottom of that cut and this is the top. ⭐ A cylinder is shaded ALONG its length, not around a centre, and the ridges follow the bands. ⛑ Rect body so the authored rotation turns the collider with it (C2b) - which is the point, a log should lie across a lane at any angle - at the known cost that the baked shadow turns too, the same trade Cart takes. ⛔ preserveAspectRatio=none is MANDATORY on the non-square viewBox (a95a2f0d). Placeholder SVG, body 2.4x0.7, blocking by definition.

name: BrokenFence
owner: C2b) - its baked shadow turns with it; preserveAspectRatio=none; NON-BLOCKING by definition
column18: ⭐ The story beat at the fence line: something came THROUGH here (broken fence + wolves in the gap). ⛔ Its enemy is not UNDAMAGED, it is UNFINISHED - a tidy gap is a gate you have not hung yet, or a panel someone carried off. Three cues carry it: a SNAPPED post still rooted, its jagged crown sitting right beside fencePost.svg's clean squared top so the eye can compare; a rail STILL NAILED at one end and swung DOWN into the gap, the one diagonal in a language made of straight parallel lines; and the PIECES STILL THERE, because removed means gone. ⭐ It has a DIRECTION - everything loose is pushed to the inside, so rotating the prop points the break the other way. ⭐ A tuft of FLEECE on a splinter is the only non-wood mark and it is what names what was taken. ⛑ Non-blocking like the Gate, and the SAME 2.0x1.6 body on the same centreline, so one authored gap takes either prop. Placeholder SVG.

It separates from house.svg on MATERIAL first and shape second: the house is a TILED GABLE (two red rectangles either side of one long ridge, straight courses ruled across), this is a THATCHED HIP (four soft straw faces to a short ridge, pale gold, no straight line anywhere). Two buildings can share a footprint and still not be confusable if they are made of different stuff. ⭐ The RAGGED EAVE is the tell a tiled roof can never have - thatch frays rather than ends, drawn as a heavy DASHED stroke round the eave line so each dash is a bundle of straw ends. ⛑ Four separate gradients, one per face, dark at the eave and pale at the ridge: a hipped roof painted flat reads as an OPEN CRATE looked into from above, which is exactly what mill.svg had to be re-cut for. ⛑ Smaller and squarer than the house (3.0x2.6 vs 4x3) - hip a long rectangle and the ridge grows until it is a gable again. Stone chimney oversized on purpose: a thatched cottage needs its fire to be visibly non-flammable. Placeholder SVG.

name: Gate
owner: C2b) - its baked shadow turns with it
column18: The break in a Fence path, and the only prop in the farm set that does NOT block - blocksMovement false, said out loud because absent means blocking. The fence is the wall, the gate is the door. ⭐ FULLY OPEN and fully passable, because a gate here is not interactable (PO 2026-09-20) so it has only two honest states - open+passable or closed+blocking - and the first draft was neither, a leaf half-swung over a gap you could walk through. The closed variant is a one-line change: swing the leaf back in line and drop the key. ⛔ The painted SWING ARC was cut (PO): real, but it drew a second banana-shaped object beside the leaf, and a gate that cannot move should not advertise the motion. What carries it now: two chunky posts on the sprite centreline with a clear gap, one bar square to the line, hinge straps, and an EMPTY latch keeper.

name: Palisade segment
owner: C2b); seamless-tiling; GENERATED by tools/make-palisade.mjs; preserveAspectRatio=none
column18: ⭐ GENERATED, and the only prop in the folder that is - because it is the only one that has to line up with a COPY OF ITSELF. The stake spacing is arithmetic, not taste, and nudging a circle to make one segment look better on its own breaks every join in the wall. ⛔ The tiling rule, both halves load-bearing: (1) the spacing STRADDLES THE SEAM - first stake half a spacing from the left edge, last half from the right, so two abutting segments put their end stakes one spacing apart like every other pair; centring a stake ON the edge doubles it at every join, a full margin leaves a gap. (2) the shadow is offset in Y ONLY, full width, square ends - an x offset cannot tile and would notch every join, so the seam wins and the light direction loses. ⭐ The art is one idea: a SHARPENED LOG TOP (four axe facets to an off-centre point), a deliberate contrast with fencePost.svg - same object, same angle, SQUARED top with end-grain rings. Squared = a fence to keep stock in; point = a wall to keep people out. Blocking. Abutting segments must SHARE a rotation.

name: Cave mouth frame
owner: C2b) - the mouth opens SOUTH; NON-BLOCKING by definition; darkness-overlay; preserveAspectRatio=none
column18: ⭐ A HOLE READS AS A HOLE BECAUSE IT HAS NO FLOOR - that is the whole problem and most of the drawing: the opening is a radial gradient to FLAT BLACK at its far edge, offset so the darkest point is at the BACK of the mouth, with no texture, no detail and no rim light. One pebble in there and it becomes a dark grey puddle. The near lip is darkened separately - the overhang's shadow falling in - and that is the depth cue. ⭐ The rock is deliberately PALE: instinct says a cave is dark, but this prop sits under Cave Air / Gloom and its job is to be FOUND, so dark rock round a black hole on dark ground is an invisible landmark. The contrast IS the signage. ⛔ NON-BLOCKING is not optional: travel fires from walking onto a named anchor (surface-west / surface-east, paired with the tunnel zone's under-*), so a blocking frame is a door that cannot be opened. ⛑ A rect collider cannot be rock-with-a-hole-in-it - wall the shoulders with a polygon or Boulders if you want them solid; this is the picture, not the geometry. The mouth opens SOUTH, so rotation aims the entrance. Placeholder SVG.
